changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 5 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6306-action-icon-type-resolution.md`

- names `action-button.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-button.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Scope is this one renderer. `type: schema` appears in exactly two files under `renderers/action/` — `action-button.tsx` (already correct) and `action-icon.tsx`; `action:group` and `action:menu` compose their members differently and are untouched.

- names `action-icon.tsx` → `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-icon.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Scope is this one renderer. `type: schema` appears in exactly two files under `renderers/action/` — `action-button.tsx` (already correct) and `action-icon.tsx`; `action:group` and `action:menu` compose their members differently and are untouched.

### `.changeset/6872-app-shell-branding-title-jsdoc.md`

- names `content/docs/guide/layout.md` → `content/docs/guide/layout.md` — edited by this change

  > Correct the `AppShellBranding.title` doc comment. It read "Page title suffix (sets document.title)" while `useAppShellBranding` assigns `document.title = title` wholesale — nothing is appended; the caller composes the whole string (the console passes `"App label — Product name"`). That comment ships in `dist/index.d.ts` and is the only description a consumer sees on editor hover, so a reader who followed it passed a suffix-only fragment and got a truncated title with no error. The comment now carries the same wording as `content/docs/layout/app-shell.mdx`, and agrees with the `AppShellProps` tables in the package README and `content/docs/guide/layout.md`. No runtime behaviour changes; the wholesale assignment and the four-surface agreement are now pinned by tests.

### `.changeset/7926-page-node-refuses-actions.md`

- names `content/docs/guide/layout.md` → `content/docs/guide/layout.md` — edited by this change

  > **Scope.** One key, by name; the node is NOT strict. A census over this tree read 91 authored `page`-tagged objects with a blind-spot reading of 8 unreadable sites, and found only `actions` (3 sites, all in `content/docs/guide/layout.md`) and `breadcrumbs` (1 site, its own question, untouched) surviving passthrough on a real `page` node — every other undeclared key belongs to a different declaration that merely spells `type: 'page'`. `PageNodeSchema` still passes unknown renderer props through.

### `.changeset/8067-component-input-member-kind.md`

- names `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` → `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > A registration's `type: 'array'` said a value was a list and stopped there, so a member that drifted from `@objectstack/spec` was invisible to every layer that reads a declaration. `page:header.actions` is the measured cost: the contract declares `z.array(z.string())` ("Action IDs"), the renderer read the members as `ActionDef` objects, and the repo-wide parity gate in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` stayed green for the whole life of the drift because both sides carried the key and neither could say what was inside it. What settled it was a maintainer ruling, not a test — and even after the fix, "these are ids" survived only as English in the registration's `description`.

### `.changeset/8871-page-node-refuses-breadcrumbs.md`

- names `content/docs/guide/layout.md` → `content/docs/guide/layout.md` — edited by this change

  > Three author sites, all teaching passages in `content/docs/guide/layout.md`, and that count **corrects the `actions` refusal's "1 site"**: its census reads every git-tracked JSON file, every `json` fence in `.md`/`.mdx`, and every TS/TSX object literal via the TypeScript AST (PR #8870), and it undercounted for **two different reasons**. The Schema API block declared `breadcrumbs?: ArrayANGLE-BRACKETS({ label, href })` outright and its literal does carry `type: 'page'`, but that literal sits inside a markdown `typescript` fence — a fence **language** the census's `json`-fence reader never visits, so it was never read at all. Best Practices §2 authored it on a fragment inside a `json` fence the census does read, but that fragment never writes `type`, so a `page`-tagged filter correctly excluded it. No example app, catalog fixture, template or customer document writes the key, so the refusal strands no authored document in this tree.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `39e625de2` (merge-base with origin/main): 9 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1801 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2409 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36702824765)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `05d9cfdfa6580d32156b3662159f75bff0fc4fe6`
Local-runs: none

Director seat (objectstack#12708, summon #30 续 2), on the standing ask 「契约复审」 and the PR's own line "the PR waits as a draft for the director seat's contract review". Inputs: card objectui#11168 (the slice plan and the objectui#11111 decision-3 = B ruling 5902351047 it cites), PR #11185 (body with its per-key verdict tables, the ten-file list, the net diff against `main` `e978ed5e` at the head), the installed contract read at its tag (`@objectstack/spec@17.5.0`, objectstack commit `e2394c448c`: `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`, the four `Action*PropsSchema` definitions, `BUTTON_PRIMITIVE_SIZES`, `actionMemberList`), objectui `main` for the `endpoint` read sites, and the check-runs on the head. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main` against the head is clean. Review faces in the diff: the `.changeset` entry and the paragraph in `content/docs/guide/layout.md`; the four renderers' registry `inputs` are the published surface under judgment; the tests are read for consistency.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set change: a widening and a narrowing of the published `inputs` of the four `action:*` blocks, each judged against the contract.** This seat extracted every top-level key of the four spec schemas at the tag and compared them with the `inputs` each renderer registers at the head:

1. **`action:button`** — the spec declares 29 keys; the PR publishes 27 of them plus `className` (a node-envelope key the console's parity guard accepts on every block, and CI's parity run is green at this head). The two not published are `endpoint` and `undoable`, exactly the pair the body holds unpublished and keeps booked to objectui#11168. **Right.**
2. **`action:icon`** — 26 declared; 25 published plus `className`; `endpoint` held. **Right.**
3. **`action:group`** — the spec's eight keys (`actions`, `display`, `location`, `label`, `icon`, `variant`, `size`, `visible`) are the PR's eight plus `className`; `name` is not published, and the spec's own guidance for this block says a group-level `name` is read by nothing and should be removed. `actions` is `z.array(z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()))` in the spec and `type: 'array', of: 'object'` in the PR; `size` is `z.enum(BUTTON_PRIMITIVE_SIZES)` = `default` / `sm` / `lg` / `icon` in the spec and the same four in the PR (so `md` is refused, as the spec refuses it). **Right, including the retirement and both narrowings.**
4. **`action:menu`** — the spec's six keys are the PR's six plus `className`; `actions` and `size` as in 3. **Right.**
5. **The `content/docs/guide/layout.md` paragraph.** "`action:button` and `action:icon` evaluate `visible` and `disabled` themselves (a boolean, a CEL string, or a `{ dialect, source }` envelope)" is the spec's `actionCondition()` describe and the renderers' `useCondition` read the body cites; "forward the action-definition keys to the runner" lists keys that are all published in 1–2; "`endpoint` is not published, because the console's `api` handler never reads it" — this seat found no `endpoint` read on any action or api path in `packages/core`, the action renderers or `apps/console` on `main`, which is the body's own measurement. **Right.**
6. **The changeset** (`@object-ui/components: minor`): the published list matches 1–4 key for key; the retired and narrowed items are named and called "breaking for an author who wrote them, which the spec already refuses"; the held pair is named with its reason. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

The body's `Clause-②` line names both directions in prose ("widens … narrows") instead of the one-arm form. Substance: the retirement of `action:group.name`, the `actions` kind and the `size` enum are a **narrowing** of this repository's published authoring surface (an author who wrote them is now refused by the manifest, the intrinsics and the page validator), so the governing arm is `(narrowing)` = BREAKING; objectui's fixed group ships a break as `minor` with the break stated in the body, which the changeset does. **Level right.** Non-blocking: the line should read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; the seat may fix it at its next push.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`action:button.size` stays `sm` / `md` / `lg`** while the spec declares `default` / `sm` / `lg` / `icon` / `md` on that block. Pre-existing, not this slice's change and not in its claim; the manifest refuses `default` and `icon` where the contract accepts them. Carrier: objectui#11168's remaining slices (the seat should book it there if it is not already).
- **`endpoint` and `undoable` are held, not decided**: a document that writes them is still forwarded at runtime and still reported `unknown-prop` by the validator; that gap is objectui#11168's open decision, stated in the body.
- **Serial on `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`** with objectui#11184 (PASS at `2b17f990`, draft): both edit the cap lines; whichever lands second re-derives the numbers.
- Draft; the seat readies and enqueues after this record.
